fixes.explanation: Nothing about flocks being held back shows up in this promise. The LORD says Pharaoh “…will allow you to leave this place,” and when he lets them go, “…he will drive you out completely.” Picture getting driven out the door while the one doing the driving yells, "Wait, leave the sheep!" That's not in the words the LORD gives.

Not quite, friend. Moses says the officials will come and bow before him, saying, “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” Think about that. These are Pharaoh's own officials, and they go from giving orders to bowing. I've had a boss change his tune before, but never that fast.

That's a sneaky little add-on, baker, but it isn't in Moses' words. He says the officials will bow and say, “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” It's a send-off with no fine print. When I got pulled out of that drawer, nobody told me to leave my edges behind either.

Not this time, friend. After Moses tells the elders the Passover words, the text says, “Then the people bowed down and worshiped.” Nobody stops to ask for proof. I think after hearing what the LORD did for their homes, bowing low just felt like the right thing to do.
